findings.issue: sortRows/defaultRows encode subtle rules — missing values always sort last, descending inverts comparison, ties fall back to move name — with no tests; a one-character change (e.g. dropping the bMissing check) would reorder every moves table silently
findings.suggestion: Extract sortRows/defaultRows into a module and add table-driven cases: nulls-last, numeric vs string keys, ascending→descending toggle, tie-break on moveName, level-up default ordering

findings.issue: Filter + pagination math (page clamping to totalPages, slice bounds, filter combination of q/type/generation) is only guarded by the acceptance suite, and the function is DOM-coupled so it can't be unit tested as written
findings.suggestion: Extract a pure filterSpecies(refs, filters) and paginate(items, page, size) and test: page beyond range clamps, page 0/negative/garbage resets to 1, combined filters AND together, empty result state

findings.issue: buildSpeciesTypeMap is the core of the home type filter and card type badges — slot ordering, duplicate suppression, and ≥10000 exclusion are all unguarded
findings.suggestion: Unit test with fixture type payloads: species with one/two types, alternate-form entries (id ≥ 10000) excluded, slots sorted so primary type is first, duplicate entries deduped

findings.issue: latestEnglishFlavor implements a spec-critical rule (last en entry, all whitespace including \f collapsed); choosing the first entry or forgetting the language filter would pass visual review and ship
findings.suggestion: Test with mixed-language entries out of order, entries containing \n/\f/\t runs, and empty input returning ''

findings.issue: prepareMoves' game ordering (api 'order' with name tie-break) and the requested-game-vs-latest fallback are data-shape-sensitive and untested
findings.suggestion: Test with version groups missing an 'order', duplicate names, ?game= pointing at an unknown group, and a Pokémon with no moves

findings.issue: The response cache's failure path — delete-on-reject so failures can be retried — is exactly the kind of logic that regresses to 'cache the rejection forever' or 'don't cache at all' without anyone noticing
findings.suggestion: Test with a mocked fetch: second call after a failed first call re-issues the request; successful responses are not re-fetched

findings.issue: The ability hidden-flag OR-accumulation over duplicate species entries is subtle (a species listed with both hidden and non-hidden varieties) and untested
findings.suggestion: Test that a species appearing twice is listed once, and whether 'Hidden ability' shows depends on an explicit rule the test pins down

findings.issue: Error routing (ApiError 404 → Not found vs any other error → also Not found but logged) has no test; a network failure being indistinguishable from a missing resource is a product decision nobody pinned down
findings.suggestion: Add a test (or at least a TODO deciding) how 5xx/network errors should render, and assert 404s show Not found

findings.issue: normalizePath's malformed-URI fallback (keeping the raw path on decode failure) and trailing-slash collapse are pure and trivially testable but aren't
mapLimit guarantees output order despite concurrent workers; the cursor++ pattern is correct now but a refactor to Promise.all(map(...)) would change concurrency semantics invisibly
findings.suggestion: Test order preservation and that no more than `limit` mappers run concurrently (counter-based test)

summary: The agent wrote no tests at all, and the code's one virtue — a clean split into pure, DOM-free helpers in api.js and data.js — makes that omission especially cheap to fix and hard to excuse. The unguarded surface includes the highest-risk logic in the app: moves-table sorting with missing values, home filtering/pagination, species-type mapping, and flavor-text extraction. Once the acceptance suite is retired, any refactor of these modules is a shot in the dark.
